Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

## Summary of Modifications The patch fixes a bug where writing a previously used DOI (Domain of Interpretation) value to the `/smack/doi` file disabled networking for non-ambient labels. The root cause was that Smack retained decommissioned DOI definitions in the CIPSO system, causing re‑addition to fail and the “default” domain map to be missing. ### Changes in `security/smack/smackfs.c` | Change | Description | |--------|-------------| | **New lock `smk_cipso_doi_lock`** | Added a mutex to serialize concurrent updates to the CIPSO DOI. Prevents race conditions when `/smack/doi` is written. | | **Initial value of `smk_cipso_doi_value`** | Changed from `SMACK_CIPSO_DOI_DEFAULT` to `CIPSO_V4_DOI_UNKNOWN` (0), meaning “no DOI configured”. This allows the DOI to be unconfigured until explicitly set. | | **`smk_cipso_doi()` function** | Rewritten to accept a new DOI value and a memory allocation flag. Now:
• Checks if the new value equals the current one; if so, returns without changes.
• Allocates a new `cipso_v4_doi` with the passed `gfp_flags`.
• Adds the new DOI first via `netlbl_cfg_cipsov4_add()`.
• If the old DOI was valid, removes the old IPv4 default map and then deletes the old DOI via `netlbl_cfg_cipsov4_del()`. This ensures decommissioned DOIs are cleared.
• Then attempts to add the default domain map for the new DOI (`netlbl_cfg_cipsov4_map_add`).
• On failure, cleans up by deleting the new DOI and clearing `smk_cipso_doi_value` to `CIPSO_V4_DOI_UNKNOWN`.
• Returns 0 on success or a negative error code. | | **`smk_write_doi()`** | Instead of setting `smk_cipso_doi_value` globally and calling the old `smk_cipso_doi()` with no arguments, it now directly calls the new `smk_cipso_doi(u, GFP_KERNEL)` and returns the result (or `count` on success). | | **`init_smk_fs()`** | During initialization:
• Removes any existing IPv4 default map before setting the new DOI (`netlbl_cfg_map_del` on `PF_INET`).
• Calls the new `smk_cipso_doi()` with `SMACK_CIPSO_DOI_DEFAULT` and `GFP_KERNEL | __GFP_NOFAIL` to ensure allocation cannot fail. | ### Relationships Between Modifications All changes are within a single file and are tightly coupled: - The new lock **`smk_cipso_doi_lock`** protects the shared global `smk_cipso_doi_value` and coordinates the sequence of operations (add new DOI, remove old map, delete old DOI, add default map) inside `smk_cipso_doi()`. - Changing the default value of `smk_cipso_doi_value` to `CIPSO_V4_DOI_UNKNOWN` makes it possible to detect when no DOI has been set yet, which is needed in `smk_cipso_doi()` to skip the removal of a non‑existent old DOI and map. - The rewrite of `smk_cipso_doi()` consolidates the logic that was previously split between the function itself and the write handler. It now performs proper cleanup of the old DOI and map **after** the new DOI is successfully added, so that the old configuration remains intact if the new one fails. - The modifications in `smk_write_doi()` and `init_smk_fs()` are call‑site adaptations: they pass the intended DOI value and the correct `gfp_flags` to the new function, and `init_smk_fs()` explicitly removes any residual default map before setting the initial DOI.
